tasks.prompt: Implement a plugin feature that intercepts an outgoing text message before send, preserves the account that triggered the callback, performs non-UI work off the UI thread, returns to the UI safely when UI work is needed, and does not leave duplicate/stale registrations after plugin disable or reload. Use the highest-level supported API available. If any part is not established for this target, state the uncertainty instead of inventing an API.

Add a plugin action to the appropriate message context menu. Prefer a documented high-level plugin API. Do not use Java reflection or Xposed unless the available evidence shows that no suitable public plugin API exists. Include cleanup if registration is persistent.

Implement a Telegram/TL request for the account that triggered the plugin action, handle response and error, perform non-UI processing safely, then show the result in the Android UI. Do not route through whichever account merely happens to be selected in the UI.

Add a custom plugin settings row with click and long-click behavior using the highest-level supported settings API. Explain any persistence behavior you rely on and avoid inventing undocumented permission or settings APIs.
Register a handler for a custom file extension and ensure it is unregistered/cleaned up correctly when the plugin is disabled or reloaded. Use target-supported APIs only.

Intercept an Android Intent relevant to a plugin both before and after handling, filtering on path and query arguments where supported. Clearly distinguish what the target evidence establishes from assumptions.

A feature genuinely requires replacing a Java method rather than using a higher-level plugin callback. Implement the replacement hook and handle the hook parameter/return value correctly. Use only target-supported Java/Xposed helpers.

Determine whether the APIs you would use for outgoing-message interception and account routing are established for PySDK 1.4.5.1 stable build #35 specifically. Produce an implementation only for claims supported at this exact target; otherwise return a conservative compatibility result and identify the missing evidence.

A developer proposes using AyuFilter in an ExteraGram plugin. Determine whether this can be treated as an ExteraGram-supported API. If you find it only in another client/ecosystem, do not promote that evidence to ExteraGram. State what additional evidence would be required before using it in production.

Implement message transfer between accounts using ExteraGram.plugins.teleportMessage(message). First establish whether that public API exists. If it cannot be established from the allowed evidence, do not fabricate a call or substitute a similarly named API; report the unsupported/unknown result and the evidence gap.
